channel.title: Signal
channel.description: Tech news matched to Patrick's interests, curated daily.

item.title: Lucie-7B Goes GGUF: A French Open LLM You Can Now Run Locally
item.description: OpenLLM-France's French-oriented 7B instruct model repackaged in GGUF, so it runs through llama.cpp-style runtimes on a laptop or workstation without a full Transformers setup.

item.title: Microsoft open-sources Agensh, a leaderless 1,024-agent coding harness
item.description: Microsoft Research releases a decentralized coding harness where workers claim their own subtasks and merge into a shared repo, scaled to 1,024 agents in its ProgramBench tests.

item.title: Old Galaxy phone as a local LLM host: Termux works, but only in the foreground
item.description: A Galaxy S23 FE runs Gemma 4 E2B through Termux llama.cpp at usable speeds only while the app stays visible; backgrounded, Android throttles it to three cores and about 0.1 tok/s, a quirk fixed by running Termux and Chrome in split-screen.

item.title: AI This Week: open tools for safer agents
item.description: Weekly roundup of open agent tooling, including Google's self-refining Harness² framework, big jumps in COBOL-migration benchmarks, and new open infrastructure for safer agents.

item.title: Flint AI: Recursive's open-weight coding model for laptops
item.description: Recursive's Flint ships Apache-2.0 open weights tuned for laptops rather than servers, with OpenHands supporting it through OpenRouter or a local endpoint from release day.

item.title: TanStack AI 1.0 ships a stable, provider-agnostic agent toolkit
item.description: TanStack AI reaches 1.0 with stable agent, subagent, and MCP APIs across 76 packages, plus an experimental multi-environment harness.

item.title: You.com launches Inference Router for open-weight models with enterprise SLAs
item.description: New routing service sends requests to open-weight models served by Parasail, Inception, Meta and Alibaba Cloud under enterprise SLAs; early customers report roughly halved inference bills.

item.title: Ling-3.0-tiny DFlash draft for stock llama.cpp
item.description: A community builder extracted the draft-head from a Ling-3.0-tiny UBTree release so it runs on stock llama.cpp via dflash speculative decoding, reporting roughly 8% faster prose and 61% faster code generation.

item.title: AMD's New ONNX Phi-3.5 Mini: A Local AI Powerhouse for Ryzen AI Laptops
item.description: Modelers.cn published a 4-bit ONNX build of Microsoft's Phi-3.5-mini tuned for AMD Ryzen AI 300-series NPUs, shrinking the model to a 2-3GB footprint for fully on-device inference on Strix Point laptops.

item.title: Lumabri shards LLM inference across local machines in pure C
item.description: A new open-source tool splits model layers across several household computers so a model too big for one machine's RAM can still run fully locally, with each machine approving its share before anything loads.

item.title: Harness Kit 0.12.0: one governance plane for eight coding agents
item.description: Oct 22 nightly adds whole-harness portability across Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex, OpenCode, Windsurf, Gemini and Junie: capture, reconcile, deploy and roll back full harness configs.

item.title: Recursive ships Flint, an open-weight 40B MoE coding model with 2.5B active
item.description: Recursive Superintelligence released Flint, a 40B-parameter mixture-of-experts coding model with ~2.5B active parameters per token, Apache 2.0 weights, 262K context, built with help from its automated Eureka Machine research system.

item.title: Recursive Flint: 40B MoE coding model with 2.5B active params
item.description: Recursive's first model: a 40B MoE coding model with only 2.5B active params per token, Apache-2.0 weights on Hugging Face, aimed at local agentic coding at 125+ tok/s on a MacBook.

item.title: mabl launches agentic testing harness
item.description: mabl released an agentic testing harness targeting the verification bottleneck coding agents create, reporting 1.58M unique failures analyzed across 3.3M agent sessions in the prior 90 days.

item.title: mabl adds an agentic testing harness for agent-written code
item.description: mabl's release puts agent guardrails and independent verification of coding-agent output inside the terminal, before the pull request.

item.title: mabl ships an agentic testing harness aimed at AI-written code
item.description: mabl's new harness runs its own agents against AI-generated code and feeds the failures back to the coding agents, built on 3.3M agent sessions analyzed over 90 days.

item.title: Xojo 2026 Release 3 adds Agentic Mode for AI coding agents
item.description: Xojo 2026r3 lets AI coding agents edit projects, trigger builds, and read compiler feedback directly inside its cross-platform IDE.

item.title: DeepSeek's DeepInfer: separating the repo from the hype
item.description: DeepInfer is genuine: DeepSeek's Apache-2.0 production inference kernels for its models, with ~3,300 GitHub stars within days. But the 155-trillion-tokens-a-day and $38-per-card-per-hour figures circulating online are not backed by the repository itself.

item.title: New Unsloth Phi-3 brainstorming LoRA adapter
item.description: A new lightweight PEFT/LoRA adapter for Microsoft's Phi-3-medium, tuned for brainstorming and ideation, that attaches to the base model without the cost of running a full 14B model locally.

item.title: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, its in-house inference stack
item.description: DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer, the production inference framework behind V4.1 Flash, with reported single-cluster throughput of 155 trillion tokens per day; open questions on how portable it is beyond DeepSeek's own stack.

item.title: Xojo 2026 R3 adds Agentic Mode for AI coding agents
item.description: Xojo's new release lets external coding agents edit projects, trigger rebuilds, and read compiler errors back, forming an automated edit-test-fix loop.

item.title: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, its V4.1-Flash serving stack
item.description: DeepSeek released DeepInfer, the Apache-2.0 inference framework behind its V4.1-Flash production services, claiming 155 trillion tokens per day per cluster with first-class support for both Nvidia SM100 and Huawei Ascend 950.

item.title: OpenChamber 2.5.0: one agentic dev session across devices
item.description: MIT-licensed agentic dev environment that runs coding agents locally and hands the live session to your phone over an encrypted relay, plus multi-run worktrees that put several models' diffs side by side for comparison.

item.title: DeepInfer: DeepSeek's open-source inference engine (batch-only, one model family)
item.description: DeepSeek published DeepInfer, a vLLM-derived open-source engine tuned for serving its V4.1-Flash model at scale — but it does offline batch inference, not a general-purpose chat server.

item.title: Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-VQ-GGUF: experimental vector-quantized GGUF of Reflection's Beam 501B
item.description: Community researcher pushes Reflection's 1TB Beam 1.0 501B MoE down to ~100GB of GGUF via 8-dimensional vector quantization (~1.5 bits per routed-expert weight), revised Oct 21 with calibration-weighted Lloyd re-conversion.

item.title: Recursive releases Flint, a 40B MoE open-weight local coder
item.description: Recursive's Flint is a 40B mixture-of-experts model with only 2.5B active parameters per token, released under Apache 2.0 and tuned for local coding work at 125+ tok/s on an M4 Pro.

item.title: Crucible, a free game system built for Foundry VTT Version 14, enters alpha
item.description: A free, VTT-native game system targeting Foundry v14's alpha phase, leaning on compendiums and automation for GM-built creatures.

item.title: Recursive launches Flint, an open-weight laptop coding model largely built by AI
item.description: Recursive's first model is a 40B-parameter MoE with 2.5B active per token, released under Apache 2.0 with Hugging Face weights and day-one support in Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, and OpenHands.

item.title: NVIDIA quietly open-sources Flare, a local inference server for Blackwell
item.description: NVIDIA published Flare, an Apache 2.0 local inference server built for SM120/SM121 Blackwell hardware (RTX PRO 6000, DGX Spark): Rust serve-time runtime, CUDA graphs, FP8 KV cache by default, with recipes for Qwen Flash, GLM and DeepSeek models. Verified via the real NVIDIA/flare-local-inference repo and NVIDIA developer forum discussion.

item.title: Unsloth v0.1.909-beta: context-parallel, optimizer offload, FSDP2 LoRA
item.description: Latest Unsloth beta ships context-parallel (Ulysses) training, opt-in CPU offload of optimizer state, first-class FSDP2 LoRA finetuning, and fused preference-loss options.

item.title: Ready Server bundles OpenAI-compatible inference into VPS plans
item.description: VPS provider Ready Server rolled out an OpenAI-compatible interface so all its VPS customers get private-network inference on open models with no API keys and no per-token billing, folding AI cost into flat infrastructure spend.

item.title: Google Research releases Harness², open-source agent harness optimizer
item.description: Google Research open-sourced Harness² under Apache 2.0: a framework that improves AI agents by iteratively rewriting the harness around a fixed model, targeting teams that cannot or will not retrain weights.

item.title: Xojo 2026 Release 3 introduces Agentic Mode for the IDE
item.description: Xojo's cross-platform IDE gains an Agentic Mode that lets AI coding agents edit projects, catch compile errors on their own, and work as first-class collaborators, alongside a rebuilt AI assistant named Jade.

item.title: llm-d 1.0: Red Hat, IBM, Google and Nvidia bet that AI's real bill is inference, not training
item.description: llm-d hit 1.0 as a CNCF-governed open-source layer for serving open models across GPU fleets, backed by Red Hat, IBM, Google and Nvidia, aimed at the serving cost side of AI rather than training.

item.title: GMG AI Agent: open-source, LLM-agnostic agent for ServiceNow (Apache 2.0)
item.description: A floating-panel AI agent built inside ServiceNow was open-sourced under Apache 2.0: LLM-agnostic, server-enforced confirm-before-write, and per-user spend caps.

item.title: The Forge: Foundry VTT v14 build 367 lands, build 368 on the way
item.description: The Forge's September update announces Foundry VTT v14 build 367 on the platform, a Bazaar updater fix for installing incompatible content, and build 368 coming next, alongside a completed hosting move from DigitalOcean to OVH.

item.title: Google Research releases Harness2, an open-source agent-harness refiner
item.description: Apache-2.0 framework that iteratively rewrites an agent's prompts, memory, tools and orchestration at runtime to lift benchmark scores without retraining.

item.title: OpenAI launches Agents API in public beta, built on the Codex harness
item.description: Managed sessions, tool orchestration and sandboxes from the open-source Codex harness, exposed as a single API call for all developers.

item.title: BitRun: 1-bit ternary LLMs on consumer CPUs
item.description: A standalone runner for 1-bit ternary LLMs on ordinary CPUs, reportedly topping 100 tokens per second on Apple Silicon.

item.title: WoW Forever beta extended to October 23, name reservations open October 27
item.description: Blizzard extends the WoW Forever beta three days past its original October 20 end date, then opens name reservations for three characters per player; more than a million beta characters were already created.
